must_remember: Electric current ($I$) is a scalar quantity defined as the rate of flow of charge: $I = \frac{dQ}{dt}$.
Drift velocity ($v_d$) of electrons in a conductor is typically of the order of $10^{-4}\text{ m/s}$, whereas thermal velocity is around $10^5\text{ m/s}$.
Current density ($J$) is a vector quantity given by $J = \frac{I}{A} = ne v_d$.
Microscopic form of Ohm's law connects current density to electric field and conductivity: $J = \sigma E$.
Mobility of charge carriers is defined as $\mu = \frac{v_d}{E}$ with SI unit $\text{m}^2/(\text{V}\cdot\text{s})$.

glossary.meaning: The rate of flow of electric charge across a cross-sectional area, measured in Amperes.
The average uniform velocity acquired by free electrons inside a conductor under the influence of an external electric field.
Electric current passing per unit cross-sectional area normal to the direction of current flow.
The magnitude of drift velocity per unit electric field for charge carriers.
The vector relation $J = \sigma E$ valid at any point inside a conducting medium.
